audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers call this EVEN at 5.5/10 with six of seven stages 'Skill'. The Emerald+ figure is 45.71% over 350 games — a real, if modest, deficit.
audit.why: The kit maths supports a slight deficit rather than a coinflip: Silver Stake scales on the health you have already lost and Purgatory is a threshold execute, so Rumble's own damage taken compounds against him, while Rumble has no dash to leave a committed exchange.
audit.corrected: Difficulty text now states 45.7% and 'slightly against you'. Left the stage sides alone — they are single words that cannot be changed inside the length band, and 'Skill' is defensible for most rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why named 'Lich Bane spike' as his first item — an item claim not supported by anything in the local data — and no spike carried a cooldown number.
audit.why: Asserting a specific item build for a champion I cannot verify a build for is speculation.
audit.corrected: Replaced with a generic first-item spike, and attached real numbers to the spikes: Ritual Nails 10/9/8/7/6s, Ashen Pursuit flat 10s at every rank, Soul Ignition 18/17/16/15/14s, Purgatory 120/100/80s at 1000 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent and one was stated backwards. (a) Soul Ignition costs Locke mana AND a percentage of his current health per second and only refunds a portion of that at the END of the duration — nothing said so, and the page actively told the player 'Anti-heal is optional'. (b) Silver Stake's on-hit magic damage is increased by the target's MISSING health, so being low is not just risky against Purgatory, it makes every one of his autos hit harder. (c) Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10 seconds at every rank, which makes the post-blink window a fixed, countable ten seconds rather than a vague 'window'.
audit.why: Riot text — Soul Ignition: 'dealing damage to himself. At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect.' Silver Stake: 'additional magic damage On-Hit, increased based on enemy missing Health.' Ashen Pursuit cooldown field: '10' with no per-rank list.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds is now stated as mandatory and timed before the end of Soul Ignition; the missing-health scaling of Silver Stake is the stated reason to stay high; the ten seconds after Ashen Pursuit is used as the concrete commit window throughout.
sources: champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json (rumble vs locke: needs-antiheal on Soul Ignition)

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. The cooldown breakdown named abilities but gave no durations.
audit.why: 'Punish the ten seconds after each spent blink' is only actionable once the reader knows the ten seconds is real and rank-independent.
audit.corrected: Added every cooldown and built the sequencing around Ashen Pursuit's flat 10s and Soul Ignition's end-of-duration refund.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t said 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal' and asserted 'his damage is AP'.
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of its source, and Soul Ignition's refund is exactly the healing worth cutting. The damage-type claim is not supported anywhere in the kit file — his passive is magic on-hit, but Q, W and R damage types are unstated.
audit.corrected: Made Grievous Wounds non-optional and tied it to the end of Soul Ignition; dropped the unsupported damage-type claim; kept the Zhonya's-class answer to the execute, which follows from R being a threshold execute.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers repeatedly describe Locke as 'a 125-range mana champ'. There is no attack-range figure in the kit file, and his ability ranges are Q 950, W 250, E 425, R 1000 — he out-ranges Rumble's 850 Electro Harpoon with two of them.
audit.why: A fabricated stat a player will plan spacing around is worse than no stat.
audit.corrected: Removed the 125 figure from tldr and phases[0].why and replaced it with the real spacing fact: he has to close to 425 with Ashen Pursuit to do his damage, while your Flamespitter needs 600.

edits.before: At 6 the stage stays even — empowered Q trades match his all-in threat — but his first item plus Purgatory is the one clear tilt in the matchup: he can execute you straight out of a telegraphed Equalizer channel. edits.after: At 6 the stage stays even — empowered Q trades match his all-in — but his first item plus Purgatory (120s) is the one clear tilt: it is a 1000-range throw that executes, so it reaches you inside a telegraphed Equalizer channel. edits.before: Post-items it evens back out: your shield answers his burst and the fight becomes a fair, repeatable exchange. edits.after: Post-items it evens back out: Scrap Shield answers his burst and the fight becomes repeatable. notes: Locke has no entry in the packet's enemyAbilities (enemyAbilities was null), so every ability name here is taken directly from champ-data/_kits/locke.json: Silver Stake (P), Ritual Nails (Q), Soul Ignition (W), Ashen Pursuit (E), Purgatory (R). The page's existing names were already right; what was wrong was the numbers and the anti-heal advice. Two fabrications removed: the repeated "125-range mana champ" (no attack-range figure exists in the kit data; his ability ranges are Q 950, W 250, E 425, R 1000) and the "Lich Bane spike" item claim in phases[5].why. One piece of advice reversed: report[8].t said "Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal". Soul Ignition explicitly heals him back a portion at the END of its duration, and Grievous Wounds cuts healing whatever its source, so anti-heal is mandatory and its timing is the whole point. LEFT ALONE AS UNVERIFIED: breakdown.cooldowns previously claimed Ashen Pursuit "resets on takedowns" — Riot's description says nothing about takedown resets, and I could not verify it, so I rewrote that bullet around the flat 10-second cooldown (which IS in the data) without asserting or denying the reset. Also unverified and untouched: the "totem"/"totem zone" wording for Purgatory (Riot calls it a binding artifact) and whether Purgatory grounds — the kit file carries a "grounding" flag but Riot's description does not mention it, so I did not write it. Rumble's Scrap Shield "knockup"/"terrain" flags and The Equalizer's "terrain" flag are misfires; _missing-interactions.json uses them to claim your kit "shuts off Locke's Ashen Pursuit" — it does not, and nothing here says so.
